prompts.text: Use the sketch tool to create an airfoil for a model plane wing, create the wing then the rest of the model so I can 3D print it.

responses.text:
I haven't built anything yet. Before I place the wing I need one number: the wingspan, in mm (for example 600 mm for a trainer-sized model, or 1000 mm for a larger one). The span decides whether the wing fits the printer and how it splits into pieces, and I have no sensible default for it.

Unless you say otherwise, I'll use these defaults:
- Airfoil: NACA 2412 (a common, forgiving model-plane section; 2% camber, 12% thick), with a chord of about 120 mm.
- Printer: 220 × 220 × 250 mm bed, 0.4 mm nozzle, 1.2 mm minimum wall.

Reply with the span, and tell me if you want a different airfoil or printer bed. Then I'll build the wing, then the rest of the model, and check each part with the printability and clearance tools.

**Problems met**
- The AskUserQuestion tool is not available in this session, so I asked in plain text instead of as a prompt.
- No geometry was written: the span is missing and has no sensible default.

The wing span is now 480 mm, up from 400 mm (+20%). Chord (120 mm) and thickness (14.6 mm) are unchanged.

Because 480 mm halves would be 240 mm, too long for the 220 mm bed, I split the wing into three pieces of 160 mm each: Wing A (y −240 to −80), Wing B (y −80 to 80) and Wing C (y 80 to 240). Each joint is a printed 4 mm dowel (four dowels in total).

Checks:
- Wing body: 120 × 480 × 14.6 mm, watertight, volume about 565 cm³ (up from 471).
- Printability still reports the whole 480 mm group as too large for the bed. The three pieces are each 160 mm, so they fit, but the checker only sees the group.
- Still unresolved: the sharp trailing edge is about 0.005–0.06 mm thick, below the 0.4 mm nozzle, flagged at five points.

Problems met
- modify.fit on the wing removed the earlier split, so I re-split the wing into three pieces.
- The wing is still solid, now about 565 cm³ (roughly 0.7 kg of PLA at 100% infill), heavier than before.

prompts.text: Span 400 mm. Go with your NACA 2412, 120 mm chord, and the 220 x 220 x 250 mm bed assumptions.

responses.text:
Built a 400 mm span NACA 2412 wing (120 mm chord) and a simple fuselage, tailplane and fin.

Parts in the scene:
- Wing (sketch-j5okmi-1): NACA 2412, 120 × 400 × 14.6 mm, laid flat with the span along Y, centred on the fuselage top (z 36). Split at Y = 0 into Wing A and Wing B (200 mm each) with two printed 4 mm dowels (Wing key 1, Wing key 2). Each half is 120 × 200 × 14.6 mm and fits the 220 × 220 × 250 mm bed.
- Fuselage (cuboid-j5okmi-5): 200 × 36 × 36 mm box, from x −100 to 100.
- Tailplane (cuboid-j5okmi-6): 40 × 140 × 4 mm, on top of the rear of the fuselage.
- Fin (cuboid-j5okmi-7): 40 × 4 × 36 mm, on the tailplane centreline.

Checks:
- Fuselage, tailplane and fin: watertight, fit the bed as placed, walls ≥ 4 mm.
- Wing: watertight. The printability check still reports an error for the whole 400 mm body, because it is one group. Each half is 200 mm in span, so it fits, but I could not check the halves separately.

Open problems:
1. The wing's sharp trailing edge is about 0.01 mm thick, below the 0.4 mm nozzle; flagged at five points. Caused by the sharp NACA trailing edge. A blunt trailing edge of about 0.4–0.6 mm would fix it; not made.
2. The wing is solid, about 470 cm³ — roughly 0.5 kg of PLA at 100% infill, too heavy for a 400 mm model. Not changed.
3. Wing halves are one group with two printed dowels; they are not separate bodies yet.
4. The fuselage is a plain box; the wing, tailplane and fin are not joined to it in the model. Glue or pins needed at assembly.

Problems met
- The first sketch call failed because atMm belongs on the curve, not in params. Fixed; succeeded.
- request and rationale are not valid on each step inside apply_records. Removed; succeeded.
- record_response was refused the first time because the prompt had not been recorded in this session. I recorded the prompt again and then saved the response.
- Wing trailing-edge wall error and whole-group size error remain (see above).
